guide.verdict: Easiest: User OAuth app, standard scopes (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none). Hardest: Public listing in Box Integrations (app review).

composio.note: Composio manages a Box OAuth app, fine for prototypes. For launch, create an auth config with your own client ID and secret, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio provides a managed Box app. Use your own app at launch if you need your branding on the consent screen, custom scopes or dedicated quota.
reasons: Managed apps show Composio's name on the consent screen
Managed default scopes may not cover what you need
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Extra Box scopes can only be requested for your own app

prerequisites.title: Box developer account
prerequisites.detail: A free developer account gives access to the Developer Console, where you create the app.

prerequisites.title: Paid enterprise account for extra scopes
prerequisites.detail: Log in to a paid enterprise account or upgrade before requesting extra scopes. Free trials cannot request them.

prerequisites.title: Public HTTPS redirect URI
prerequisites.detail: At least one redirect URI is required; it must be HTTPS (plain HTTP only for localhost) and match exactly.

steps.title: Create a User app in Developer Console
steps.detail: Choose New App, select User as the app type (OAuth 2.0), then Create.

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio dashboard
steps.detail: Take the callback URL from the Composio dashboard and check it is HTTPS.
steps.done_when: Redirect URI is ready to register.

steps.title: Register redirect URI and scopes
steps.detail: Add the redirect URI in the OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI section and enable only needed scopes before any admin authorizes the app.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create an auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret from the Configuration tab.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists for the box toolkit.

steps.title: Give Client ID to customer admins
steps.detail: Where an enterprise requires it, its Box Admin enters your Client ID in the Admin Console Platform Apps tab.
steps.done_when: The app shows as enabled for that enterprise.

steps.title: Draft use-case justification for scope
steps.detail: Write why the use case requires the scope, since Box approves only on that basis.

steps.title: Open support ticket for the scope
steps.detail: Submit the request through Box support from a paid enterprise account.

steps.title: Wait for Box decision
steps.detail: Box reviews each request individually; no timeline is documented.
steps.done_when: Box approves or declines the scope.

steps.title: Submit app for Box Integrations listing
steps.detail: Use the Developer Console submission flow and complete Box's checklist.

steps.title: Wait for partner review
steps.detail: If silent after a week, file a ticket so Box can try to expedite.

traps.title: The general per-user API limit is 1000 API requests
traps.detail: The general per-user API limit is 1000 API requests per minute per user; the page says these limits apply to all Box user accounts and does not tie them to app approval status.

traps.title: The upload limit is 240 file upload requests per
traps.detail: The upload limit is 240 file upload requests per minute per user.

traps.title: Box Sign create and resend sign request calls are
traps.detail: Box Sign create and resend sign request calls are limited to 100 requests per minute per user; get sign request calls are limited to 1000 requests per minute per user.

traps.title: A newly created enterprise can authorize up to 10,000
traps.detail: A newly created enterprise can authorize up to 10,000 custom apps.

traps.title: A developer token generated by hand in the Developer
traps.detail: A developer token generated by hand in the Developer Console is meant for development only.

traps.title: Customer admin authorization can be slow
traps.detail: A Box advocate said Box cannot speed up admin-side authorization of a custom app; a developer thread cites 15-20 days.

traps.title: Scope changes need re-authorization
traps.detail: Changing scopes or access level requires re-authorization, which an enterprise Box Admin must do.

traps.title: App type cannot be changed
traps.detail: An OAuth 2.0 app cannot become a Server app; you must create a new app.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: Mismatched or missing redirect_uri causes errors such as redirect_uri_missing.

traps.title: Custom app calls count toward customer's quota
traps.detail: Calls from custom apps count toward the customer enterprise's monthly API allocation; partner integrations do not.

blockers.what_it_means: Their enterprise leaves unpublished apps inactive by default.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask their Box Admin to add your Client ID in Admin Console.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the instructions for the admin.

blockers.symptom: Extra scope request is declined or unavailable
blockers.what_it_means: Box found the use case does not require the scope, or the account is not eligible.
blockers.what_to_do: Narrow the scope request or use a paid enterprise account.

open_questions: How long does a Box Integrations listing review take, and what triggers it? Ask Box developer support.
